extracted.intended_audience: practitioners/respondents, counsel, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, standards, and factors governing service, default, findings of misconduct, and penalties in USPTO (OED) disciplinary proceedings, as applied in an Initial Decision on Default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO Rule 11.35 provides that a complaint may be served on a respondent by: (1) delivering a copy personally; (2) mailing a copy by 'Express Mail,' first-class mail, or any delivery service that provides ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery; and, for respondents who reside outside the United States, by sending a copy by any delivery service that provides ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery (including to a nonregistered practitioner's last address known to the OED Director).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of shipment and delivery receipts (e.g., FedEx notifications) establish adequate service of process. The rule contemplates ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery; the decision relied on FedEx International Priority shipping and delivery records to conclude adequate service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for answer (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An answer to a complaint shall be filed within the time set in the complaint but in no event shall that time be less than thirty days from the date the complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints will specify the filing addresses and the deadline (minimum 30 days). In the decision, the thirty-day period from the complaint's filing date was computed as the deadline for filing an answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default judgment / admission (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations in the complaint and may result in entry of default judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default may be entered without a separate motion for default; the Rules do not require that a motion for default be filed nor that any period be provided to respond to such a motion. A respondent's explicit statement of intent not to answer supports entry of default; upon default the allegations are deemed admitted and findings may be based on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing officer's control of motion response timing (37 C.F.R. § 11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer will determine the time period for filing a response to a motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the hearing officer generally sets response times, in a motion for default where the respondent has not appeared, it is not necessary to allow an extended period for response; the decision treats such discretion as consistent with promptly entering default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not 'Engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations that a practitioner failed to provide or report knowledge or evidence to OED in an investigation can constitute conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice under this subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not 'Engage in any other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word 'other' requires that conduct charged under (b)(6) be distinct from conduct prohibited by 10.23(b)(1)-(5); the same facts cannot support separate findings under both (b)(5) and (b)(6). (See Moatz v. Colitz.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful refusal to reveal or report knowledge (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct which constitutes a violation of paragraphs (a) and (b) includes, but is not limited to: (16) Willfully refusing to reveal or report knowledge or evidence to the Director contrary to § 10.24 or paragraph (b) of § 10.131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations that a practitioner knowingly failed to provide requested information to OED or intentionally failed to cooperate with an investigation fall within this enumerated example of prohibited conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of default on findings of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: When a respondent is found in default, the respondent is deemed to have admitted all of the allegations in the complaint, and findings and conclusions may be rendered based on those admitted allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default prevents development of a fuller record respecting circumstances; thus, factual findings in a default decision are based on complaint allegations and supporting exhibits rather than contested testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty determination factors (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining any penalty the following factors shall be taken into consideration: (1) Whether the practitioner has violated a duty owed to a client, to the public, to the legal system, or to the profession; (2) Whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) The amount of the actual or potential injury caused by the practitioner's misconduct; and (4) The existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four factors guide sanction selection (e.g., reprimand, suspension, exclusion). The decision cites intentional and knowing failure to cooperate and prior disciplinary history as aggravating considerations supporting exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of exclusion as sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the PTO is appropriate when misconduct offends core ethical standards (e.g., candor and truthfulness), including knowingly failing to provide requested information, purposefully misleading OED, intentionally failing to cooperate, and when aggravating factors (such as prior discipline) are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tribunal may consider the respondent's explicit choice not to answer charges, the likely waste of government resources if a sanction hearing were pursued, and precedent (courts imposing disbarment for failure to cooperate) when imposing exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent on 'other' conduct (interpretive constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: To give the word 'other' significance in § 10.23(b)(6), the facts alleged to constitute a violation of § 10.23(b)(6) must be other than facts alleged to constitute violation of another provision of Section 10.23(b)(1)-(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision cites Moatz v. Colitz and uses this interpretive rule to conclude that the facts in the complaint support only a violation of § 10.23(b)(5), not both (b)(5) and (b)(6). This prevents double-counting the same misconduct under multiple subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure and consequences of non-appeal (37 C.F.R. § 11.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appeal from an Initial Decision issued pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.54 must be filed with the Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline within 30 days after the date of the Decision and must include exceptions to the Administrative Law Judge's Decision and supporting reasons therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file such an appeal in accordance with § 11.55 will be deemed both acceptance of the Initial Decision and waiver of rights to further administrative and judicial review. The decision references the proper filing address per 37 C.F.R. § 1.1(a)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-exclusion responsibilities and reinstatement references (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 & 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's attention is directed to § 11.58 regarding responsibilities in the case of exclusion and § 11.60 concerning petition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sections set out obligations while excluded and the process/requirements for seeking reinstatement; the decision orders exclusion and notifies the respondent of these regulatory avenues.
